item.title: Boerne Champion falls to Austin Westlake in boys water polo state final
item.description: Boerne Champion teammates console each other after falling to Austin Westlake at the UIL State Water Polo Championship game at at the Josh Davis Natatorium in San Antonio on Oct. 24, 2026. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) Boerne Champion is in the midst of a prolific run of five straight boys water polo state tournament appearances. But a state championship still eludes the Chargers. Boerne Champion fell to Austin Westlake 15-8 Saturday afternoon at Josh Davis Natatorium in the UIL state championship match. "It's a success because we haven't made it to that game in two years," said Boerne Champion head coach Scott Slay when reflecting on the Chargers' season. "To make it back, that's the accomplishment and relief the boys had." While Boerne Champion has qualified for state every season since 2022, the Chargers missed out on the state title match the last two years. Boerne Champion got past League City Clear Creek in Friday's state semifinals, and got a measure of revenge in taking out the team that eliminated the Chargers from last year's state tournament. But the Chargers had another familiar foe standing in their way. Boerne Champion entered Saturday's match 0-2 all time against Westlake, including a 9-5 loss in non-district play Sept. 19. "Westlake is one of the best teams I've seen in the last 25 years," Slay said. Boerne Champion's Julius Hoxhaj protects the ball during the UIL State Water Polo Championship game at at the Josh Davis Natatorium in San Antonio on Oct. 24, 2026. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) Boerne Champion was held scoreless in the entire first half as Westlake jumped to an 8-0 lead at the halftime break. The Chargers took 28 shots compared to the Chaparrals' 33, but had some misfortune at the net as multiple shots clanked off the bar. "The bar is not your friend and turnovers kill you," Slay said. "And that's what happened." Boerne Champion got on the board with 4:30 left to play in the third quarter with a goal by senior utility player Grant Perkins, who took advantage of a power play. The Chargers outscored the Chaparrals 8-7 in the final two quarters, but the scoreless first half was too much for Champion to overcome. "I think they came out a little nervous," Slay said of the first half. "Looking at our second half, we were probably the better team in the second half. So I think nerves got them." Slay also credited Westlake for their defensive efforts on senior utility player Julius Hoxhaj, the reigning Express-News Boys Water Polo Player of the Year. Hoxhaj led Boerne Champion in scoring with four goals on Saturday afternoon, but Westlake consistently had two defenders on him. "Other kids stepped up," Slay said. "We had some good goals." Perkins scored three goals before Hoxhaj put the ball in the net with 1:41 to play in the third quarter. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) Boerne Champion is in the midst of a prolific run of five straight boys water polo state tournament appearances. But a state championship still eludes the Chargers. Boerne Champion fell to Austin Westlake 15-8 Saturday afternoon at Josh Davis Natatorium in the UIL state championship match. "It's a success because we haven't made it to that game in two years," said Boerne Champion head coach Scott Slay when reflecting on the Chargers' season. "To make it back, that's the accomplishment and relief the boys had." While Boerne Champion has qualified for state every season since 2022, the Chargers missed out on the state title match the last two years. Boerne Champion got past League City Clear Creek in Friday's state semifinals, and got a measure of revenge in taking out the team that eliminated the Chargers from last year's state tournament. But the Chargers had another familiar foe standing in their way. Boerne Champion entered Saturday's match 0-2 all time against Westlake, including a 9-5 loss in non-district play Sept. 19. "Westlake is one of the best teams I've seen in the last 25 years," Slay said. Boerne Champion's Julius Hoxhaj protects the ball during the UIL State Water Polo Championship game at at the Josh Davis Natatorium in San Antonio on Oct. 24, 2026. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) Boerne Champion was held scoreless in the entire first half as Westlake jumped to an 8-0 lead at the halftime break. The Chargers took 28 shots compared to the Chaparrals' 33, but had some misfortune at the net as multiple shots clanked off the bar. "The bar is not your friend and turnovers kill you," Slay said. "And that's what happened." Boerne Champion got on the board with 4:30 left to play in the third quarter with a goal by senior utility player Grant Perkins, who took advantage of a power play. The Chargers outscored the Chaparrals 8-7 in the final two quarters, but the scoreless first half was too much for Champion to overcome. "I think they came out a little nervous," Slay said of the first half. "Looking at our second half, we were probably the better team in the second half. So I think nerves got them." Slay also credited Westlake for their defensive efforts on senior utility player Julius Hoxhaj, the reigning Express-News Boys Water Polo Player of the Year. Hoxhaj led Boerne Champion in scoring with four goals on Saturday afternoon, but Westlake consistently had two defenders on him. "Other kids stepped up," Slay said. "We had some good goals." Perkins scored three goals before Hoxhaj put the ball in the net with 1:41 to play in the third quarter. Junior utility player Landon Muenchow also scored a goal for the Chargers with 6:28 remaining in the final quarter. "They've really matured and they're just a great group of kids to be around," Slay said of this year's team. "And sometimes it's bigger than the game." Boerne Champion finishes the season at 25-4, while Westlake caps its championship run at 30-1. Westlake senior defender Luke Welton was named the game's MVP and led both teams in scoring with six goals. As Boerne Champion looks ahead to next year for another opportunity at its first state title, Slay believes water polo in the Greater San Antonio area will only get better. "The future's bright in San Antonio," he said. "San Antonio is closing the gap." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Valkyries win might put WNBA in 'unavoidable' arena issue for Finals Game 6
item.description: Kiah Stokes #41 of the Golden State Valkyries and Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream compete for the opening tip-off in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on Oct. 24, 2026 in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The Golden State Valkyries went into Atlanta for two WNBA Finals games and got a split by knocking off the Dream 67-62 on Saturday. Now, with this best-of-seven series tied at two, the biggest question from before the series has returned: where, exactly, will Game 6 be played? The Dream have called Gateway Center Arena in College Park home for the last six seasons, which only has a capacity of around 3,500. But the Dream have moved every playoff game this year to the much larger State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, an arena operated by the NBA's Hawks that holds a little more than 17,000. Once the WNBA Finals matchup was set, it wasn't clear where the league was going to hold the three games in Atlanta. The WNBA set the Finals schedule months in advance with national television partners, and State Farm Arena had conflicts for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6. But on Oct. 13 , the WNBA announced that Games 3 and 4, the two guaranteed-to-be-played games in Atlanta, would be moved in order to get them played in State Farm Arena. Left unsaid, though, was what would happen if the series went to the sixth game, which is currently scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 28. The league still hasn't answered that question by Saturday's tip time, but a Hawks executive has taken people inside the negotiations. Atlanta Hawks chief operating officer Steve Koonin went on 92.9 The Game, Atlanta's sports talk radio station on WZGC-FM, on the " Dukes and Bell " show on Friday and was asked about Game 6 and gave a rather ominous quote. "To be 100% clear, the decision is the league's. We do not have a decision," Koonin said. "We have made multiple dates available. I am hoping Dream in five, I am praying Dream in five, I am walking around with my legs, fingers, toes crossed for Dream in five. But that's a league decision. It's very hard to move NBA games. "So write your local congressman and commissioner that we play. Because they need to be in a major - this is high-level basketball - to be in a professional building." Koonin said Game 6 going to the much smaller Gateway Center Arena "might be unavoidable" because of the complex scheduling issues, particularly because the Hawks are scheduled to face the Cavaliers that night. "You can't go move a Cleveland game without affecting 10 other games. It's dominoes," Koonin said. "I'm hopeful, but we're having lots of discussions and telling the league what's going on in Atlanta. The Dream are top of mind, people are excited - they blew the roof off. I hope the Dream are inside [State Farm Arena], and if not, we're going to fight like hell for them to be in our building. We've made dates available to the league." item.content:encoded: Kiah Stokes #41 of the Golden State Valkyries and Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream compete for the opening tip-off in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on Oct. 24, 2026 in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The Golden State Valkyries went into Atlanta for two WNBA Finals games and got a split by knocking off the Dream 67-62 on Saturday. Now, with this best-of-seven series tied at two, the biggest question from before the series has returned: where, exactly, will Game 6 be played? The Dream have called Gateway Center Arena in College Park home for the last six seasons, which only has a capacity of around 3,500. But the Dream have moved every playoff game this year to the much larger State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta, an arena operated by the NBA's Hawks that holds a little more than 17,000. Once the WNBA Finals matchup was set, it wasn't clear where the league was going to hold the three games in Atlanta. The WNBA set the Finals schedule months in advance with national television partners, and State Farm Arena had conflicts for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6. But on Oct. 13 , the WNBA announced that Games 3 and 4, the two guaranteed-to-be-played games in Atlanta, would be moved in order to get them played in State Farm Arena. Left unsaid, though, was what would happen if the series went to the sixth game, which is currently scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 28. The league still hasn't answered that question by Saturday's tip time, but a Hawks executive has taken people inside the negotiations. Atlanta Hawks chief operating officer Steve Koonin went on 92.9 The Game, Atlanta's sports talk radio station on WZGC-FM, on the " Dukes and Bell " show on Friday and was asked about Game 6 and gave a rather ominous quote. "To be 100% clear, the decision is the league's. We do not have a decision," Koonin said. "We have made multiple dates available. I am hoping Dream in five, I am praying Dream in five, I am walking around with my legs, fingers, toes crossed for Dream in five. But that's a league decision. It's very hard to move NBA games. "So write your local congressman and commissioner that we play. Because they need to be in a major - this is high-level basketball - to be in a professional building." Koonin said Game 6 going to the much smaller Gateway Center Arena "might be unavoidable" because of the complex scheduling issues, particularly because the Hawks are scheduled to face the Cavaliers that night. "You can't go move a Cleveland game without affecting 10 other games. It's dominoes," Koonin said. "I'm hopeful, but we're having lots of discussions and telling the league what's going on in Atlanta. The Dream are top of mind, people are excited - they blew the roof off. I hope the Dream are inside [State Farm Arena], and if not, we're going to fight like hell for them to be in our building. We've made dates available to the league." When asked if the Valkyries would have to sign off of a schedule change again, Koonin replied, "We all play when we're told." This week in Atlanta, Game 3 was held on Wednesday, one day earlier than it was previously scheduled to be played. And Saturday's Game 4 was moved up by 2.5 hours to make it part of a doubleheader at State Farm Arena. The Dream game was played at 1 p.m. local time in Atlanta, with the Hawks' home opener later that night pushed back by half-an-hour to 8:30 p.m. Eastern to ease the transition from one team to the other. Koonin celebrated how both games were sold out in the interview on 92.9 The Game. Earlier in the call, Koonin was discussing the "amazing" crowd the Dream drew at Game 3 and expressed his hope for Atlanta to win on Saturday. Koonin was clearly hoping the Dream would win on Saturday and wrap up the series in San Francisco on Monday to make all of the arena discussions a moot point for Game 6. Unfortunately for Koonin, though, the Valkyries played their best game of the series on Saturday, racing ahead to a double-digit lead in the second quarter and keeping any Dream runs contained in the second half. The series will continue in San Francisco on Monday with Game 5 on Monday, with tipoff scheduled for 5 p.m. Pacific. Game 6 is now guaranteed to be played and is currently scheduled for Thursday at 8 p.m. Eastern in Atlanta. Pakistan won their first two matches, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 runs, while England lost their two matches with a two-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka even after managing to score 429/4 in their last match. item.title: Chris Sutton says Arsenal’s big squad has helped them again
item.description: Chris Sutton says Arsenal’s big squad has helped them again Chris Sutton has praised Arsenal’s squad depth after the Gunners defeated Everton , just days after Bukayo Saka suffered a long-term injury. The former striker believes Mikel Arteta has enough quality in his squad to cope with the winger’s absence and continue collecting important points. Saka has been one of Arsenal’s most influential players, so news that he would be sidelined for two months raised concerns among supporters. His creativity and attacking contributions have made him a key figure, leaving questions about how the team would perform without him. However, Arsenal have quality alternatives in several positions, giving Arteta options to adjust his starting eleven. Their first test following Saka’s injury came against Everton, providing an opportunity to show they could still deliver without one of their biggest stars. Arsenal demonstrate their squad depth David Moyes has beaten Arsenal several times during his managerial career and arrived in North London hoping to secure a positive result. However, the Gunners proved too strong, producing an assured performance to claim all three points. The victory demonstrated that Arsenal can remain competitive without Saka. Although replacing his quality is difficult, the squad has capable players who can help maintain the team’s standards during his absence. Sutton believes this strength in numbers played an important role in the result, allowing Arteta to make changes without significantly weakening his side. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Sutton praises Arsenal’s options Speaking via BBC Live , Sutton highlighted the importance of having reliable replacements available when key players are injured. “It’s about squad depth and Arsenal have shown today changes which they’ve made, with Bukayo Saka being injured and out for a while, but they have players who can come in and may not be as effective but still enough to get over the line. A big three points.” The victory offers encouragement to Arteta as he prepares for the coming fixtures. If his alternatives continue to deliver, Arsenal can manage Saka’s absence without allowing it to derail their campaign. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Chase Briscoe Wins Pole for Talladega’s YellaWood 500
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez Chase Briscoe delivered a strong qualifying performance on Saturday, securing the pole position for Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver put his No. 19 Toyota at the top of the leaderboard, earning a crucial starting position as the championship battle enters another important weekend. Briscoe posted a lap at 186.065 mph, completing the 2.66-mile superspeedway in 51.466 seconds. His effort narrowly edged Austin Hill, who qualified second with a speed of 185.949 mph. The difference between the two drivers was just 0.032 seconds, making it a close battle for the top starting spot. The pole marks Briscoe’s first of the 2026 season at Talladega and the 10th of his NASCAR Cup Series career. It also gives the No. 19 team another reason to feel confident heading into a race that could have significant championship implications. Briscoe has enjoyed success throughout the Chase, including victories at Las Vegas and Charlotte. He also enters the weekend as the defending winner of the fall Talladega race, giving him an opportunity to repeat that performance in front of the Alabama crowd. The Indiana native currently sits third in the championship standings, 24 points behind leader Kyle Larson. With only three races remaining, every stage point and finishing position could make a difference in determining who advances toward the championship. Starting up front does not guarantee success at Talladega, where drafting, aggressive moves and large multi-car accidents can dramatically change the race. However, Briscoe has positioned himself to take advantage of the opening laps and potentially collect valuable points early. Austin Hill will join Briscoe on the front row, while Trackhouse Racing teammates Connor Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen qualified third and fourth, respectively. Chris Buescher rounded out the top five. Several championship contenders will have more ground to make up. Larson qualified 10th, while Joey Logano will start 16th, Chase Elliott 18th and Ryan Blaney 27th. Tyler Reddick, who won at Phoenix last weekend, qualified 33rd. Sunday’s YellaWood 500 is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET on NBC. With the championship battle tightening, Briscoe will look to turn his pole position into another victory and close the gap on Larson in the standings.

item.title: OKC Thunder waive Otega Oweh following season-ending torn Achilles tendon
item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder made their first roster move of the 2026-27 regular season. And it's one that shouldn't be a shocker to anybody. They have waived Otega Oweh. He was on a two-way contract. This was purely a roster mechanism move. Oweh sustained a torn Achilles tendon in OKC's preseason. So it was only a matter of time before the Thunder moved on to open up the roster spot. The 23-year-old was the No. 41 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. It sounds like the Thunder will add Micah Peavy to Oweh's two-way spot. He was a 2025 NBA draft second-round pick. The Memphis Grizzlies waived him as part of their final roster cuts. Now, he lands in OKC. An all-time setback for Oweh. Before he even had the chance to make his NBA debut, he was sidelined for an entire year. He will miss the entire 2026-27 season recovering from his torn Achilles tendon. Maybe the Thunder will give him a chance to re-earn a two-way spot next summer. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: OKC Thunder waive Otega Oweh following season-ending torn Achilles tendon

item.title: Lions plan massive Brian Branch decision for Packers matchup
item.description: Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Lions plan massive Brian Branch decision for Packers matchup appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions (3-2) reportedly plan to activate star safety Brian Branch ahead of Sunday’s Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers (4-2) , setting up his long-awaited return from a torn Achilles. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler shared the development Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter, while reposting a hype video released by Detroit. “Lions plan to activate safety Brian Branch, who returns nearly 11 months from his Achilles tear. He’s set to make his season debut Sunday vs Packers,” Fowler wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Branch has been sidelined since suffering a torn Achilles during Detroit’s Week 14 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 4, 2025. The injury occurred while he attempted to break up a pass in the end zone. The 25-year-old subsequently missed the remainder of the 2025 campaign and began the 2026 season on the physically unable to perform list . Lions plan to activate safety Brian Branch, who returns nearly 11 months from his Achilles tear. He’s set to make his season debut Sunday vs Packers. pic.twitter.com/E72oKVcICd — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 24, 2026 Brian Branch’s return provides major boost to Lions’ secondary Before suffering the injury, Branch appeared in 12 games last season, recording 75 total tackles, including five tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, nine passes defended and one forced fumble. Branch’s return provides Detroit with a significant reinforcement in its secondary as the team prepares for an important NFC North matchup. The former Alabama standout earned Pro Bowl honors in 2024 after recording 109 tackles, four interceptions and 16 passes defended across 16 games. Detroit also appears prepared to give Branch a substantial workload in his season debut, with defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard indicating the team does not plan to impose a strict snap count. The Lions will look to improve to 4-2 when they host the Packers on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Related: Packers Week 7 injury report vs. Lions: Are Christian Watson, Matthew Golden injuries cause for concern? Related: Lions’ Dan Campbell accuses reporters of making Sam LaPorta situation a ‘distraction’

item.title: Naji Marshall Steps Up As Dallas Mavericks’ New Enforcer
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The most surprising thing about Naji Marshall’s Friday night performance wasn’t his 15 points or three steals. It was the fact that he ran from half court to confront a teammate’s attacker and picked up a technical for it. Marshall proved he is the physical shield the Dallas Mavericks need right now. He did not back down from a hard foul that left a young star injured on the floor. During the second quarter, Aaron Nesmith committed a rough foul while trying to block a dunk attempt by Cooper Flagg. Flagg was in mid-air and had no way to protect himself when Nesmith hit him. The impact caused Flagg to injure his left shoulder, the same one that troubled him last year. Marshall saw the play and immediately ran over to Nesmith to demand answers. The two players had to be pulled apart before the situation got worse. Both men received double technical fouls for the heated exchange. Defending the Team First Marshall is known for being protective of his teammates throughout his entire career. According to The Smoking Cuban , he is not a hothead who looks for fights, but he will not tolerate nonsense. He ran from the other side of the court to stand up for Flagg, who is seen as a young superstar for the franchise. Marshall is now fully adopting the enforcer role the Mavericks require from him, as this action demonstrates. He made it clear that no one goes after his friends without consequences. Although P.J. Washington possesses this protective quality as well, reports indicate Marshall could be an even stronger enforcer than Washington. The Smoking Cuban noted that Marshall is notoriously protective of teammates and that he isn’t going to let anyone hurt his friends. This mindset is crucial for a team that wants to win a championship. A squad needs players who will stand up for each other when the refs miss a call or a rival plays dirty. Marshall delivered that message loud and clear on Friday night. A Public Promise of Loyalty After the game, Marshall took to social media to show his loyalty to the team. He posted a message on X stating he would stand up for Flagg and anyone else wearing a Mavericks uniform. The post included a direct quote where he said, “I got you 32…any # on this side tbh!!!! #1stoneeeeeeeee LETS KEEP IT GOING MY BROTHASSSSS!!!!!!!!!!!” This public declaration reinforces the idea that he is the guy Dallas fans can trust to handle the physical side of the game. RotoWire reported that Marshall finished with 15 points and three steals in the 121-105 win over the Pacers. He played 33 minutes and helped secure the team’s first win of the season. The Mavericks now have a player who is ready to take a charge for his teammates. Marshall’s stats were solid, but his willingness to get into trouble for the team is what matters most. According to The Smoking Cuban, he got into Nesmith’s grill and likely exchanged some choice words with him. That kind of fire is rare to find in the modern NBA.

item.title: How Indiana's 'gritty' OT victory at Michigan tilts CFP, Big Ten title race in favor of Hoosiers
item.description: How Indiana's 'gritty' OT victory at Michigan tilts CFP, Big Ten title race in favor of Hoosiers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Indiana had not won at Michigan Stadium since 1967. In somewhat fitting fashion, the Hoosiers beat the Wolverines in a game straight out of the '60s. No. 6 Indiana beat Michigan 13-6 in an overtime slugfest that will be huge for the Hoosiers later. "Regardless of how pretty it was, it was gritty," Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said on the Fox telecast. "It was gritty as hell. It's a win, and we're going to celebrate it." Indiana's Josh Hoover led the go-ahead TD drive in overtime, and the Hoosiers' defense held on against Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr. How did the Hoosiers win? What does this mean for the Big Ten race and the College Football Playoff MORE: Sporting News 2026 Midseason All-America college football team Josh Hoover battles through rough start vs. Michigan Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, who played through right arm and wrist injuries, struggled against the Wolverines' defense for much of the game. The Hoosiers (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) led 6-0 at halftime behind a pair of Nico Radicic field goals, but Hoover was 7 of 16 for just 60 yards. He threw just one pass in the second half of regulation, which resulted in a Zeke Berry interception that set up a 29-yard field goal by Trey Butkowski with 2:22 remaining in the fourth quarter. Indiana grounded out tough yardage with Turbo Richard (19 carries, 68 yards) and Lee Beebe Jr. (12 carries, 56 yards), but the Hoosiers went back to the passing game on the first play of overtime. Hoover hit tight end Brock Schott on a deep in route for a 12-yard gain, then the quarterback scrambled for a 4-yard TD run and the game's only touchdown. Hoover finished 8 of 18 for 81 yards and an interception, but he made clutch plays similar to those in the 20-17 victory at Nebraska on Oct. 10. The TCU transfer, however, did deliver the first victory at the Big House in nearly 60 years. item.title: Ravens Week 7 injury report vs. Bengals: Lamar Jackson’s status puts Baltimore offense in limbo again
item.description: Image Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Ravens Week 7 injury report vs. Bengals: Lamar Jackson’s status puts Baltimore offense in limbo again appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens enter Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals with their biggest offensive question still unanswered. Lamar Jackson is questionable with an ankle injury after participating on a limited basis in all three practices, leaving Baltimore to prepare without certainty at quarterback. Jackson’s practice involvement keeps a return possible, but the report offers no confirmation that he will play. His availability remains the central storyline for an offense that must account for both his passing ability and the pressure his mobility puts on opposing defenses. Baltimore’s official player page documents Jackson’s ankle injury and his recent progression back to limited practice. That provides context for his participation, but it does not settle his availability against Cincinnati. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lamar Jackson’s questionable status leaves Baltimore balancing two plans Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Jackson’s Wednesday, Thursday and Friday designations followed an identical pattern: limited participation. There was no listed setback, but there was also no upgrade to full participation before the final injury report. That distinction matters. Taking practice snaps and handling an entire game are different demands, particularly for a quarterback whose movement can influence nearly every defensive decision. If Jackson plays, Baltimore must determine how much of its offense he can comfortably execute. Designed quarterback runs, pocket escapes and throws outside the original play structure all place different demands on an injured ankle. The concern is not simply whether Jackson can take the opening snap. It is whether he can protect himself, maintain his mechanics and respond when protection breaks down. If he cannot play, Baltimore would need an approach suited to its replacement quarterback rather than expecting the same offensive possibilities. Either scenario makes preparation more complicated, with the final decision still unresolved. Mark Andrews practiced fully throughout the week despite a hand injury and carries no game designation. Ravens receive encouraging updates around their uncertain quarterback The supporting cast offers considerably more stability than Jackson’s designation might suggest. Mark Andrews practiced fully throughout the week despite a hand injury and carries no game designation. Rashod Bateman progressed from limited participation Wednesday to full sessions Thursday and Friday while managing a shoulder injury. Matthew Hibner followed that same progression with a hand issue. Baltimore also received encouraging participation from several offensive linemen. Guards Olaivavega Ioane, John Simpson and Andrew Vorhees each moved from limited work Wednesday to full participation over the final two practices. None received a game designation. Center Cam Jurgens practiced fully all week despite appearing on the report with a concussion and likewise has no game designation. Ronnie Stanley’s week requires a more careful reading. Listed with rest, toe and ankle concerns, he went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday before missing Friday. However, he has no game designation. Those developments give Baltimore fewer listed availability concerns elsewhere on offense, even as its quarterback situation remains unsettled. Defensive absences add pressure against Cincinnati Baltimore has already ruled out safety Jaylinn Hawkins and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson. Hawkins missed the final two practices with a knee injury, while Robinson did not practice all week because of a pectoral injury. Cornerback T.J. Tampa is doubtful after three limited practices with a knee issue. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington is questionable following the same participation pattern because of an ankle injury. There are brighter spots. Trey Hendrickson practiced fully throughout the week despite a finger injury and has no game designation. Calais Campbell also has no designation after a rest-related practice schedule. The defensive absences could narrow Baltimore’s options for rotations and substitutions. Combined with Jackson’s uncertain availability, they leave the Ravens facing important personnel decisions on both sides of the ball before kickoff against a divisional opponent, with limited margin for further disruption. item.title: Seahawks turn to practice squad for defensive depth, bring Anthony Bradford back from IR
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos completes a catch against Trevon Diggs #16 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are on a two game losing streak, set to host the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs at Lumen Field on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City comes in with former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker carrying enough of the load to allow All-Pro quarterback Patrick Mahomes to ease his way back from knee surgery, while the Seattle defensive front is facing a host of injury questions heading into the game. Zach Charbonnet, Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt have been ruled out, while DeMarcus Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu, Connor O’Toole are all questionable. With only seven inactives available and one reserved for the emergency quarterback, that leaves just three inactive slots for the five players who are questionable. Depending on Drew Lock’s health, it is entirely possible that Jalen Milroe could be the backup for the Seahawks Sunday, with Lock slotted into the emergency quarterback role. Given the uncertainty of the available depth, it comes as no surprise that Seattle turned to the practice squad Saturday afternoon, elevating linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo and defensive back Trevon Diggs to the active roster for the matchup against the Chiefs. Today’s @Seahawks roster moves: https://t.co/rdtBJCxCLZ — Seahawks PR (@seahawksPR) October 24, 2026 The Seahawks also activated right guard Anthony Bradford from injured reserve, making room for Bradford by waiving receiver Montorie Foster Jr.

Depending on Drew Lock’s health, it is entirely possible that Jalen Milroe could be the backup for the Seahawks Sunday, with Lock slotted into the emergency quarterback role. Given the uncertainty of the available depth, it comes as no surprise that Seattle turned to the practice squad Saturday afternoon, elevating linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo and defensive back Trevon Diggs to the active roster for the matchup against the Chiefs. Today’s @Seahawks roster moves: https://t.co/rdtBJCxCLZ — Seahawks PR (@seahawksPR) October 24, 2026 The Seahawks also activated right guard Anthony Bradford from injured reserve, making room for Bradford by waiving receiver Montorie Foster Jr.

item.title: ‘I don’t think LeBron’s a total disgrace’: Skip Bayless defends LeBron James from President Trump
item.description: Skip Bayless has spent much of his career as one of LeBron James’ harshest critics. But when it comes to President Donald Trump’s latest attacks on the Philadelphia 76ers star, even Bayless is coming to James’ defense. In a conversation with Stephen A. Smith, Bayless pushed back on Trump calling James a “total disgrace” over his behavior during the national anthem. While Bayless called James “the ultimate diva,” he said that James has been “a very good role model” off the court, and suggested that Trump’s comments are about politics. Trump vs. LeBron Before the Sixers’ season opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday, video shared by ClutchPoints showed James swinging his arms as if practicing a golf swing during the national anthem, then going through his shooting motion. The moment drew backlash from conservative pundits, and on Thursday, Trump demanded an apology on Truth Social. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote. Later that day, Trump mocked James’ golf swing during a rally, calling it “a big scandal kind of a story.” James brushed off the criticism after the Sixers’ comeback win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night. “Must (have been) a slow news day at the office, you know? Slow news day in the office,” James said, via USA Today . ‘The Ultimate Diva’ Bayless, a longtime critic of LeBron, didn’t exactly let the NBA superstar off the hook for the moment itself as he called LeBron “the ultimate diva.” “I don’t think LeBron is deeply sort of psychologically wanting to protest the anthem. I think LeBron is, you know, he is the ultimate diva, and he’s earned a lot of his divaness,” Bayless said in a clip shared on X . “But he wants during the anthem to do a look at me. Remember, I’m LeBron James, and I’m here with my new team, and I’m going to be doing my golf swing during the anthem because I want to differentiate myself from these teammates of mine.” However, he did argue that Trump is simply taking advantage of a long-running feud. “What has Trump’s MO been from the start? He says, if you don’t like me, I don’t like you. And LeBron’s made it clear from the start he doesn’t like President Trump,” Bayless said. “So President Trump is going to leap through every little cracked door that LeBron cracks for him.” And Bayless made it clear that he thinks Trump went too far. “But to go total disgrace, I don’t think LeBron’s a total disgrace and bad guy. I don’t. And I’m not a fan of LeBron’s as a basketball player per se, but off the court, to your point, he has been a very good role model,” Bayless said. “And this is just politics.” Bayless even suggested that Trump might have “some deeper level of respect” for James, and that the timing of the attacks isn’t a coincidence. “I just think to your point, it’s midterms. That’s what’s happened,” Bayless said. The post ‘I don’t think LeBron’s a total disgrace’: Skip Ba

item.title: GAME THREAD: Washington State welcomes No. 21 Boise State for Homecoming
item.description: CORVALLIS, OR - OCTOBER 17: Players of the Washington State Cougars huddle during the first half of a game between the Washington State Cougars and the Oregon State Beavers at Reser Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Corvallis, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Good afternoon, Cougar football fans. It’s Homecoming weekend on the Palouse, and the Washington State Cougars face off with the No. 21 Boise State Broncos. WSU (1-6, 0-3 in Pac-12) began the second half of the 2026 season down in Corvallis, Oregon against the Oregon State Beavers last week and lost their fourth straight game, 48-30. In that game, WSU started a different quarterback, redshirt freshman Owen Eschelman. In his collegiate debut, Eschelman provided the Cougar offense a jolt that they desperately needed. In the last three prior games, WSU had scored just three offensive touchdowns. Against OSU, Eschelman had three himself. Two through the air and one rushing. He finished the game 32 for 49 in pass attempts for 289 passing yards and one interception that came very late in the game. He also had 15 total rushing attempts for another 136 yards. He will again get the start today. BSU (5-1, 2-0) is riding high off five straight wins and is off a bye week. In their last game two weeks ago, the Broncos defeated the Fresno State Bulldogs 38-31 in Fresno, California, to bring the Milk Can back to Boise for the first time since 2022. If WSU is going to pull off the upset, they will need Eschelman to continue to elevate the offense like he did last week. They will also need to find a way to efficiently run the football. Last week, Cougar running backs had 13 rushing attempts for 26 yards. That’s not going to cut it. Boise State’s run defense is vulnerable, though. The Broncos are giving up five yards per rush attempt on the season. What isn’t very vulnerable for the blue and orange has been their incredibly efficient offense. The Bronco offense won’t beat you over the top with many explosive plays, but they will grind their way down the field. They rank in the top 30 in success rate, power success, and stuff rate. The most telling stat for this Bronco offense is their time of possession. The Broncos lead FBS in time of possession percentage at 60.23%. WSU’s defense is going to have to find their way off the field early in Bronco possession, not just to prevent them from scoring, but to make sure they are too fatigued late in the game. Kickoff is at 3:00 p.m. and it couldn’t be a more perfect day for Cougar football in Pullman. It should be about a crisp 54 degrees at kickoff with very few clouds in sight and some slight wind. Go Cougs!

item.title: Couple Badgers starters on injury report, while USC has 6 players out, 3 questionable
item.description: Austin Kawecki #51 of the Wisconsin Badgers lines up over the football at the line of scrimmage against the Western Illinois Leathernecks at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin, on September 12, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are taking on the No. 16 USC Trojans at Camp Randall Stadium on Saturday night, looking to bounce back from their 17-7 loss to the No. 12 UCLA Bruins last weekend. The Badgers were on a four-game win streak going into last weekend and were expected to be fresh coming off their bye. The defense stood up to the challenge, stopping one of the best rushing attacks in the NCAA, but they did struggle to defend third downs in the passing game. USC, on the other hand, is coming off their bye week after an impressive 31-23 road win over Penn State, easing some of the tension from head coach Lincoln Riley. The Trojans are 6-1 this season, with their lone loss being to Oregon. But USC hasn’t been convincing in any of its recent wins, and they’re now heading on the road into another tough environment in Madison. Heading into Saturday, we’ve got a loaded injury report on both sides. For the Badgers, there are only five players with a ‘probable’ or ‘questionable’ diagnosis. Starters Javan Robinson, Darrion Dupree, and Austin Kawecki are probable, while running back Nate Palmer and wide receiver Malachi Coleman are questionable. Wisconsin opened the week with Robinson and Coleman as questionable. Robinson was finally upgraded to probable on Friday, while Coleman remains questionable. Kawecki has been probable all week. Dupree wasn’t on the injury report on Wednesday, but popped up on Thursday and Friday, although he was still listed as probable on both days. Palmer started the week as doubtful, but was upgraded to questionable on Thursday and Friday. USC’s side is more of an issue. The Trojans are without wideout Terrell Anderson, wideout Corey Simms, safety Kendarius Reddick, linebacker Taylor Johnson, linebacker Roman Marchetti, and Kilian O’Connor. Where things get more interesting is the questionable section, as tight end Mark Bowman, wideout Luc Weaver, and defensive tackle Jide Abasiri are all questionable for the game, while Jahkeem Stewart and Jaydn Walker are questionable. Getting Bowman, a five-star true freshman, back for the Trojans would be huge. Former Wisconsin transfer Tucker Ashcraft could be the starter if Bowman remains out, as he’s been the last two games. Elsewhere, Weaver saw an uptick in role with Anderson and Simms up for the season. He’s questionable. Abasiri is also a key cog for the Trojans up front. Stewart, a former five-star and another much-needed player for USC, should play on Saturday night.

item.title: Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier
item.description: Brazil legend Ronaldinho will make his playing return aged 46 next month for Ravenna, the third-division Italian club announced on Saturday. The 2002 World Cup winner’s move to Ravenna was announced in June. He is aiming to score his 300th career goal. The former Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker retired in 2015, 10 years on from claiming the Ballon d’Or and has become a shareholder in Ravenna, situated between Venice and San Marino. “The wait now has a date: Sunday, November 15,” Ravenna said in a statement. “The Brazilian legend will wear the Ravenna FC shirt in the derby against Forli. “An event that will turn the eyes of the world toward the Bruno Benelli Stadium.” Ravenna are second in Group B of the Italian third tier, six points below leaders Spezia and are aiming for a return to Serie B for the first time since 2008. Vanguard News The post Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: MN Twins Legend Drawing Managerial Interest
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect This week has generated some significant headlines from the former Minnesota Twins department. Mitch Garver officially stepped away from the game, and Kurt Suzuki won’t be brought back as manager of the Los Angeles Angels. Of course, that new managerial opening paves the way for a fresh hire. We have already heard plenty about the Seattle Mariners’ interest in former Twins manager Rocco Baldelli. It’s logical that the Angels could show interest as well. Beyond Baldelli though, there’s former Minnesota star Torii Hunter, who, like Suzuki, happened to play for Los Angeles. Hunter was someone the MN Twins could have turned to, but they instead hired Derek Shelton last offseason. He has been closely linked to the Angels since playing there, and now the new ownership group could come calling. Torii Hunter in play for Los Angeles Angels job Last October, Torii Hunter ’s name came up as a potential managerial candidate for the Minnesota Twins. Declan Goff (SKOR North) reported that he turned down an opportunity to interview with the franchise, but Hunter later said he went after both the Twins and Angels jobs. He was a finalist in Los Angeles before the Angels moved on and gave Kurt Suzuki a one-year deal. Former Twin Torii Hunter, 51, who also played five seasons for the LA Angels, is expected to receive serious interest in the Angels managing vacancy. Charley Walters – Don’t Print That Charley Walters (Don’t Print That) reports that Hunter should receive serious interest from the Angels once again. He has operated in a special assistant capacity with the organization, but his future role remains uncertain with John Mozeliak having taken over as interim general manager after Perry Minasian was fired in June. There’s also the complicating factor that Stan Kroenke has agreed to buy the franchise from Arte Moreno, with the sale expected to become official in early 2027. With multiple moving pieces, it’s hard to predict how the team will operate going forward. Hunter is a logical fit though. Over the course of his 19-year career , he played five seasons with Los Angeles after spending the first 11 with Minnesota. With the Angels he was a two-time All-Star and two-time Gold Glove winner. Now 51 years old, Hunter would be looking at his first managerial job at any level. Is LA a better job than the MN Twins? Neither team hired Hunter last fall, and the landscapes are wildly different. The Angels went 62-100 during Suzuki’s only year at the helm, the first 100-loss season in franchise history. They also haven’t made the playoffs since 2014 and have consistently produced losing records. Minnesota finished this season with a 77-85 record while fighting against a lackluster overall roster. Charley Walters – Don’t Print That Charley Walters (Don’t Print That) reports that Hunter should receive serious interest from the Angels once again. With multiple moving pieces, it’s hard to predict how the team will operate going forward. Hunter is a logical fit though. The Angels went 62-100 during Suzuki’s only year at the helm, the first 100-loss season in franchise history. The Angels have consistently spent more than the MN Twins, but tend to get less out of it. Hunter may find allure in coaching future first-ballot Hall of Famer Mike Trout through the end of his contract (2030), but Trout isn’t the same difference maker at this point. Los Angeles needs a talent infusion both at the major league level and throughout the farm system. For someone who would be managing for the first time in their career, it’s a tough ask to expect an immediate turnaround. Hunter did play the role of leader very well for the 2015 Twins , who were coming off four straight 90-loss seasons. Dance parties aren’t the only thing that will get the Angels back on track though. item.title: No. 20 Maryland women’s basketball holds on vs. No. 12 North Carolina, 72-68, in back-and-forth exhibition
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - FEBRUARY 25: Oluchi Okananwa #7 of the Maryland Terrapins shoots a free throw against the Northwestern Wildcats at Xfinity Center on February 25, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images No. 20 Maryland women’s basketball was tied with No. 12 North Carolina five times over the course of the Terps’ final exhibition game of the season, with neither team able to break away and obtain a stable lead. With only four seconds left, Addi Mack headed to the free throw line with a chance to ice the game. Mack made both to push the Terps into a two-possession lead. Tar Heel Nyla Brooks fired off a 3- pointer to close the game, but missed the net entirely, handing Maryland its second exhibition win, 72-68. The Tar Heels broke through the Terps’ defense in the first quarter, pulling away with a 10-4 lead. Stanford transfer Nunu Agara managed to briefly pull Maryland out of its deficit, sparking a run before making a fast break layup to tie the game at 13 apiece. Agara went on to score 15 of Maryland’s 32 first-half points and finished with a 22-point, 11-rebound double-double that she credited to her new team. “The passion comes from just playing for my teammates,” Agara said, “They’re my sisters, and I want to do well.” Oluchi Okananwa gave Maryland its first lead of the day. With less than a minute left in the first quarter, the senior stole the ball around mid court and banked a jumper from the paint. Just seconds later, she made a layup on the back of Chloe Sotell’s defensive rebound. Addi Mack briefly returned to shooting glory with her first 3-pointer of the day in the first seconds of the second quarter. When the Terps faced off in the postseason against the Tar Heels, Mack went 3-for-5 from outside the arc. The sophomore didn’t attempt another deep ball for the rest of the game, though. McDaniel’s layup put the Terps back up, 26-25, halfway through the second quarter. After a North Carolina jumper, sophomore Maria Boiko restored the lead just a minute later. After logging her first defensive rebound, the Belarusian forward splashed a second-chance pull up shot for her first points of the season. Maryland created several opportunities for points on the back of turnovers but couldn’t finish them. Redshirt freshman Lea Bartelme dove for the ball to force a turnover and passed to freshman Trinity Jones to score a layup, but Jones couldn’t complete the shot. Maryland dominated the paint in the first half, outscoring North Carolina in the paint, 20-8. The Terps also outrebounded North Carolina 23-18, allowing just one first-half offensive rebound. Head coach Brenda Frese said Agara needed to do a better job anchoring the defense after the Terps allowed 40 points in the paint and 18 offensive rebounds against Virginia Tech on Monday. After logging her first defensive rebound, the Belarusian forward splashed a second-chance pull up shot for her first points of the season. Maryland created several opportunities for points on the back of turnovers but couldn’t finish them. Redshirt freshman Lea Bartelme dove for the ball to force a turnover and passed to freshman Trinity Jones to score a layup, but Jones couldn’t complete the shot. Maryland dominated the paint in the first half, outscoring North Carolina in the paint, 20-8. The Terps also outrebounded North Carolina 23-18, allowing just one first-half offensive rebound. Head coach Brenda Frese said Agara needed to do a better job anchoring the defense after the Terps allowed 40 points in the paint and 18 offensive rebounds against Virginia Tech on Monday. Those numbers dropped to 26 and seven, respectively, on Saturday. Meanwhile, Jones flourished in the second half. The freshman made consecutive baskets at the beginning of the third quarter for her first points of the game, pushing Maryland ahead, 36-33. Jones, the No. 9-ranked recruit according to 247Sports , finished with nine points, four rebounds and three assists. “[Jones] just plays the right way,” Frese said. “Her motor just never gives up….[Jones] just wants to be on the court and help her team win.” Rainey Welson notched her first points of the season with just two minutes left in the third quarter. The sophomore guard connected on a pair of 3-pointers from the corner to push the Terps out to their largest lead of the game, 54-48. Midway through the fourth quarter, Jordyn Jackson took a pass from Jones, and the freshman-to-freshman connection led to a 3-pointer that cushioned the Terps’ five-point lead. Jackson’s shot was met by a jumper from Tar Heel Noelle Bofia, assisted by her top-ranked freshman teammate, Kate Harpring. Harpring gave Maryland’s defense problems all game, finishing with a game-high 29 points and six rebounds. Maryland’s free throws made up the difference, though. The Terps notched 19 shots from the line, accounting for more than a quarter of their total points. “Free throw shooting is always going to be really important to us,” Frese said after the game. “I love, just, the way we were able to be aggressive.” Through the last three minutes, the Terps and Tar Heels chased each other up and down the court without a shot to show for it. While Maryland didn’t make a field goal in the final four minutes, it was perfect from the free-throw line down the stretch to seal a tight victory. Frese said playing a basketball powerhouse like North Carolina in an exhibition game was intentional in preparing for the season ahead. “We don’t have time to make sure that everyone’s comfortable and confident,” Frese said in a preseason press conference. “We can get those jitters and nerves worked out and do it at a really high level.” Three things to know 1. Reversing history. Maryland’s win over North Carolina was its first since 2013, when the Terps won 85-59. They had lost their previous three matchups against the Tar Heels, including a second-round loss that ended the Terps’ 2025-26 season. 2. Maryland can win in multiple ways. After a high-scoring win over Virginia Tech, Maryland toppled North Carolina in a defensive battle. Agara held down the paint with 11 rebounds and two blocks. Okananwa led the team with three steals, and the Terps forced 11 turnovers. 3. The underclassmen stepped up in the clutch. Down the stretch, second-year players Bartelme and Mack knocked down the big free throws. Bartelme had the ball in her hands a lot down the stretch and was tasked with breaking the North Carolina full-court press. Sophomore Rainey Wilson closed the third quarter with two straight 3-pointers, and freshman Jordyn Jackson hit a clutch 3-pointer to extend the lead to five points with just over five minutes left in the game.

item.title: Golden State Valkyries Tie WNBA Finals At 2-2 With Game 4 Win
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 24: Tiffany Hayes #15 and Kaila Charles #6 of the Golden State Valkyries react during the fourth quarter in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream at State Farm Arena on October 24, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Images The Golden State Valkyries stole a 67-62 road win over the Atlanta Dream to even the WNBA Finals series at 2-2, shifting home-court advantage as the series heads back to the Bay Area for game five. The Valkyries were led by the three-headed monster of Gabby Williams (17 points), and 13 points a piece by Veronica Burton and Tiffany Hayes. Additionally, off the bench Cecilia Zandalsini contributed 10 points. Further, Kiah Stokes recorded a career-high 16 rebounds, but her biggest impact came on the defensive end. She helped limit Angel Reese to just eight points after the Atlanta Dream star posted 30- and 21-point performances in Games 2 and 3, respectively. Stokes said of her role and responsibility guarding Reese, “She has been the head of their snake all series. For me, it was trying to make every look she had at the basket difficult. It is a tough job, but I think being our best defensive big, I have to own up to that challenge.” ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 24: Angel Reese #5 of the Atlanta Dream dribbles against Kiah Stokes #41 of the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on October 24, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Specifically, the defensive intensity of the Valkyries caused the Dream to turn the ball over 17 times, and generated eight steals. Further, the Dream were held to 33% shooting from the field, and 17% from beyond the arc. The Valkyries also had 38 points in the paint compared to Atlanta’s 28 points, and seven fast break points compared to just two points from the Dream. This might be one of the most important details of the game, as Atlanta typically likes to move through a quick, transition based, down hill offense. ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 24: Rhyne Howard #10 of the Atlanta Dream shoots the ball against Kiah Stokes #41 of the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on October 24, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. We are definitely enjoying this win, but nothing was won or lost here in Atlanta, so we definitely have to take care of home court.” She continued, “As far as turnovers, that has been our bread and butter all season, we were kind of out of character game two and three so getting back on track.” Williams also attributed their defensive adjustments to the win in game four, “I am sorry if I sound redundant but we kept our ball pressure, I think that we were a bit more connected today and that gives us our energy.” ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 24: Rhyne Howard #10 of the Atlanta Dream shoots the ball against Veronica Burton #22 of the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter in game four of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on October 24, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Dream outscored the Valkyries 19-12 in the third quarter and 17-13 in the fourth, with forward Rhyne Howard leading the comeback effort. Howard scored 11 of her 19 points in the fourth quarter, but Atlanta ultimately came up short. In the presser after the game Dream head coach Karl Smesko stated, “Give them credit, they came out super aggressive, they were crashing the boards, they were being very aggressive on defense and we just needed to take care of the ball better, get some better shots early.” He elaborated, “I am really happy with the fight we showed in the second half, but we can’t put ourselves in that position where you are playing a defensive team and you are having to come back from double figures.” The WNBA Finals will move to game five on Monday, October 26 back in Balhalla at 7pm EST on USA Network, CNBC, and streaming on Peacock. item.title: Former West Boca star Javian Mallory big part of offense in Canes' win
item.description: No. 1 ranked Miami defeated Pittsburgh 52-23 on Saturday afternoon at Hard Rock Stadium and Javian Mallory was once again a big part of the offensive explosion. While receiver Malachi Toney stole headlines with a career performance, Mallory, a former West Boca Raton High School standout running back, rushed for 47 yards and two touchdowns on seven carries for the 7-0 Canes. One of those scores was an 11-yard powerful run up the middle in which Mallory showcased a little Le'Veon-Bell-esque stutter-step before he hit the hole on his way to the end zone. TOUCHDOWN HURRICANES! 🔥 Javian gets it done on the ground 🙌 pic.twitter.com/V4uB0qYaSY — Miami Hurricanes Football (@CanesFootball) October 24, 2026 Mallory was an annual Palm Beach Post first-team All-County football selection and committed early to Miami. Thus far in his freshman season, he has 444 yards and seven scores. The performances against Pitt followed another two-touchdown performance on 108 yards rushing against FSU, a game that went to double overtime before UM won. He is the team's leading rusher through seven games. Miami played in the 2026 College Football Playoff National Championship game, losing to Indiana. Mallory was present in uniform, although he did not play. This year, he would be part of the team seeking to go one step farther. Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@gannett.com. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Former West Boca star Javian Mallory big part of offense in Canes' win

item.title: Beyond the home run: The art of timely hitting
item.description: Although one of the best clutch teams in the game, the Tampa Bay Rays failed with runners in scoring position on Friday night, going 0-for-6 vs. the Brewers. | (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) As the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays battle for a World Series title, Chicago’s struggles with runners in scoring position reveal an offensive weakness the White Sox must address. The Rays spent six months making runners in scoring position (RISP) a strength. On Friday night, six missed opportunities helped turn their 2026 World Series opener into a loss. Tampa Bay went 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position against the Brewers, falling 3-2 despite advancing the tying run 90 feet from home in the ninth inning. A team that led Major League Baseball with a .283 batting average in those situations suddenly found itself searching for one more productive swing. “We had traffic on the bases pretty much all night,” Rays shortstop Taylor Walls told MLB.com . “But [we] weren’t able to get that big hit, that timely hit, the double with a runner on first or a single with runners in scoring position.” More than 1,200 miles away, the White Sox could recognize the frustration. Chicago’s postseason ended against Cleveland with a different statistical problem but a similar consequence: Runners never reached home plate. The White Sox hit .243 with RISP during the regular season, ranking 22nd in the majors. They struck out 397 times in 1,361 official at-bats in those situations, a 29.2% K-rate. By comparison, Tampa Bay hit .283 with RISP, while Milwaukee followed at .276. Both clubs combined consistent contact with aggressive baserunning, providing a different offensive model than Chicago’s power-oriented lineup. The problem became particularly evident during the American League Division Series. Although the White Sox hit .275 with runners in scoring position across seven postseason games, they struck out 21 times in 51 at-bats with RISP. Cleveland pitchers struck out 75 Chicago hitters during the five-game ALDS, including an all-time record of 21 in the decisive Game 5. Manager Will Venable acknowledged that the problem extended beyond chasing pitches outside the strike zone, to misses in the zone, and his assessment revealed a fundamental challenge: Against elite pitching, even hitters making reasonable swing decisions can struggle to produce contact. That becomes particularly costly with a runner on third and fewer than two outs, as a sacrifice fly or a well-placed ground ball can score a run without a hit. A strikeout, however, leaves the runner exactly where he started. Modern hitting philosophies emphasize power, patience and avoiding unnecessary outs. Those principles have merit, but postseason baseball frequently demands a more situational approach. Milwaukee demonstrated that on Friday. item.content:encoded: Although one of the best clutch teams in the game, the Tampa Bay Rays failed with runners in scoring position on Friday night, going 0-for-6 vs. the Brewers. | (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) As the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays battle for a World Series title, Chicago’s struggles with runners in scoring position reveal an offensive weakness the White Sox must address. The Rays spent six months making runners in scoring position (RISP) a strength. On Friday night, six missed opportunities helped turn their 2026 World Series opener into a loss. Tampa Bay went 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position against the Brewers, falling 3-2 despite advancing the tying run 90 feet from home in the ninth inning. A team that led Major League Baseball with a .283 batting average in those situations suddenly found itself searching for one more productive swing. “We had traffic on the bases pretty much all night,” Rays shortstop Taylor Walls told MLB.com . “But [we] weren’t able to get that big hit, that timely hit, the double with a runner on first or a single with runners in scoring position.” More than 1,200 miles away, the White Sox could recognize the frustration. Chicago’s postseason ended against Cleveland with a different statistical problem but a similar consequence: Runners never reached home plate. The White Sox hit .243 with RISP during the regular season, ranking 22nd in the majors. They struck out 397 times in 1,361 official at-bats in those situations, a 29.2% K-rate. By comparison, Tampa Bay hit .283 with RISP, while Milwaukee followed at .276. Both clubs combined consistent contact with aggressive baserunning, providing a different offensive model than Chicago’s power-oriented lineup. The problem became particularly evident during the American League Division Series. Although the White Sox hit .275 with runners in scoring position across seven postseason games, they struck out 21 times in 51 at-bats with RISP. Cleveland pitchers struck out 75 Chicago hitters during the five-game ALDS, including an all-time record of 21 in the decisive Game 5. Manager Will Venable acknowledged that the problem extended beyond chasing pitches outside the strike zone, to misses in the zone, and his assessment revealed a fundamental challenge: Against elite pitching, even hitters making reasonable swing decisions can struggle to produce contact. That becomes particularly costly with a runner on third and fewer than two outs, as a sacrifice fly or a well-placed ground ball can score a run without a hit. A strikeout, however, leaves the runner exactly where he started. Modern hitting philosophies emphasize power, patience and avoiding unnecessary outs. Those principles have merit, but postseason baseball frequently demands a more situational approach. Milwaukee demonstrated that on Friday. Christian Yelich drove home Jackson Chourio with a first-inning triple, William Contreras followed with an RBI single, and Chourio added a two-out RBI single in the seventh. The Brewers went 2-for-8 with runners in scoring position, but those hits helped secure a one-run victory. Milwaukee scored 832 runs during the regular season despite hitting only 154 home runs. Chicago hit 211 homers but scored 776 runs. The Brewers also stole 162 bases compared with Chicago’s 93, demonstrating another way to create offensive pressure. Those differences suggest the White Sox do not necessarily need to abandon power. They need a more balanced offensive approach. That balance has been an organizational question throughout the past decade, as Chicago has cycled through rebuilding rosters, veteran lineups and postseason contenders. The 2026 results provide another reason to examine whether the club has consistently struggled to convert scoring opportunities. For players such as Colson Montgomery, Kyle Teel and Miguel Vargas, improvement must include producing quality plate appearances against elite pitching. Montgomery’s power remains valuable, but the White Sox need consistent contact throughout the lineup. Free agency could provide additional options. Luis Arráez offers a contact-oriented offensive profile, while potential free agents Bo Bichette, Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki represent different combinations of hitting ability and overall production.Simply acquiring a hitter with a high RISP average, however, would not guarantee improvement. Tampa Bay’s World Series opener demonstrated that even baseball’s most productive situational hitters can struggle when opportunities arise. Rays manager Kevin Cash remained confident despite the loss. “This is an extremely confident group,” Cash said . “They’re going to be fine.” Chicago’s challenge is finding that same confidence while developing the offensive consistency needed to advance deeper into October. The White Sox proved they could hit enough home runs to reach the postseason. Cleveland demonstrated that power alone was not enough to survive it. And as Milwaukee showed Friday, sometimes the difference between winning and losing isn’t the ball that leaves the park. It’s the one that brings the runner home.

item.title: Germany's Struff stuns Fils to reach European Open final in Brussels
item.description: FILE PHOTO - German tennis player Jan-Lennard Struff reacts during his men's singles quarter-final match against Italy's Jannik Sinner on Day Nine of the 2026 Wimbledon Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. (is associated with: «Germany's Struff stuns Fils to reach European Open final in Brussels») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff claimed a surprise win over France's Arthur Fils to book a spot in the European Open final in Brussels. Struff prevailed 6-4, 6-7 (7-9), 7-6 (7-5) and will face Dutch Tallon Griekspoor in Sunday's final. The German, who reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals in July, is now into his first ATP Tour final since his title run on home soil in Munich in 2024. "I want to thank the crowd for the support. It was an unreal match," Struff said following his victory. "I felt I played a very, very good first set, he won the second set which was very close. I managed to come back from a break down twice in the third set. I am just very happy to get the win."

item.title: Raheem Morris Sends Clear Message To Falcons Before Sunday
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Raheem Morris is back in Atlanta, but he is not here to hug the fans. He is here to break Michael Penix Jr. The former head coach now runs the defense for the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. They arrive on Sunday, Oct. 25, with a 6-0 record. The Falcons sit at 2-4 and need a win to stop the bleeding. Morris knows every weakness in this roster. He helped build it. That history makes this matchup dangerous for Atlanta. Shanahan Rejects The Revenge Angle People love a good revenge story. They think the 49ers will play extra hard just to beat their old boss. That is not how this group works. Kyle Shanahan shut down that idea on Thursday. He told reporters that his team is already focused on winning every single game. “I don’t think they can be more motivated,” Shanahan said, according to the Sumter Item . He added that the players care about Morris but will not treat this as a personal game. Fred Warner backed him up, saying every week feels like the biggest week of their lives. This is a team that does not get distracted by feelings. The 49ers defense has 15 sacks so far this season. They have nine sacks in just the last two games. They are coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium to pressure Penix. The quarterback was sacked five times last Sunday against the Bears. He lost a fumble too. Morris knows exactly where to hit him. The 49ers want to keep their perfect record alive. They will not let emotions get in the way of a clean win. Penix Knows The Stakes The young quarterback sees the challenge clearly. He knows Morris is waiting for him with a trap. “It’s going to be exciting,” Penix said, according to Chattanooga Times Free Press . He added that it will be good to see Morris again, but the team must find a way to score. “We got to find a way to obviously put points on the board against his defense.” Penix is 2-2 as a starter this year. He has had to deal with rib injuries and a surgically repaired knee. He has been sacked nine times in four games. Despite the struggles, Morris still has high praise for the kid he drafted. He spoke warmly about Penix on Thursday. “Loved the kid, loved everything about him,” Morris said. He talked about Penix’s personality and his throwing ability. Morris believes the quarterback is healthy and ready. But loving a player does not mean letting him play easy. Morris will use that knowledge to design plays that hurt the Falcons. The offense must handle the pressure or this game ends early. The Undefeated Streak Hangs In The Balance The 49ers have not lost a game yet. They are 6-0. The Falcons have lost two in a row. The gap between these teams is huge right now. Morris spent two years as the Atlanta head coach. He went 16-18 and got fired. He knows the playbook. He knows the players. He knows the front office. item.title: Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager
item.description: Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction. Saints began the campaign with the points penalty after spying on opposition training sessions, which also cost them the chance of promotion in the play-off final last season. Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin all struck before half-time for the visitors, who are now within three points of the automatic promotion places. Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top. “This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes. “They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.” Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone. Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge. “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement. “The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.” Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road. Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places. Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places. AFP The post Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Clashes Break Out In Paris, Other French Cities Amid Fresh Protests
item.description: Clashes broke out Saturday in Paris and other French cities amid demonstrations held a week after others that degenerated into street violence and prompted a robust security backlash as President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order. Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers were confronted with “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Riot squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes. Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case. Authorities had deployed 70,000 security forces across the country for the new marches, which were called to protest the cost of living. Protesters hold antifascist banners and flags as they face CRS riot police in a street by the Campo Santo Antifascist village set as part of a counter-mobilisation “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the congress of the far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France, on October 24, 2026. (Photo by SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP) The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over a country that goes to the polls in six months to choose a successor to President Emmanuel Macron after 10 years. Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses. There was nevertheless widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as repressive and as an assault on the right to protest. Police battle ‘rioters’ Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union. The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources. Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones. The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”. In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully. The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities. Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march.
